entities.summary:
Johannes de Garlandia was a French music theorist of the late ars antiqua period of medieval music. He is known for his work on the first treatise to explore the practice of musical notation of rhythm, De Mensurabili Musica.

De Garlandia's contributions to music theory had a lasting impact on the development of Western classical music. His work on rhythm and meter influenced later composers such as Hildegard von Bingen and Guillaume de Machaut.

The publication of De Mensurabili Musica in the late 13th century helped to establish music as a respected discipline within the medieval university system. This, in turn, paved the way for the growth of musical institutions and the development of new musical styles.

In recent years, De Garlandia's work has been recognized as a significant milestone in the history of music notation. His innovative approach to rhythm and meter has been praised for its clarity and precision, and his treatise remains a fundamental text in the study of medieval music theory.

'In De Mensurabili Musica, we find the seeds of a new understanding of rhythm and meter, one that would go on to shape the course of Western classical music for centuries to come.'
